sampling_model.design: Known independent unit-level \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment on a fixed partition into unequal disjoint cliques.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) units, partition, graph, exposure map, and all exposure-indexed potential outcomes are fixed.
sampling_model.treatment: Within block \(l\), All Treat and All Control are mutually exclusive events, each with probability \(q_l=2^{-r_l}\); blocks are independent.
sampling_model.overlap: Every target exposure has known positive probability \(q_l\), which may vary with \(l\) and vanish along triangular arrays.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No superpopulation nuisance is estimated; on a unanimous block, the observed block mean equals the corresponding fixed-schedule block mean, and omitted blocks receive deterministic bias protection.
sampling_model.randomness: The only inferential randomness is \(Z\), augmented by independent \(R\) solely to include externally randomized interval procedures in the decision class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Exposure-weighted estimators are unbiased, conservative randomization variances are available, and local-dependence conditions justify asymptotic normal intervals.

Section 4.3 constructs finite-sample Hoeffding-type confidence intervals for population-average direct, indirect, total, and overall effects of binary outcomes under a two-stage partial-interference design.

Exact confidence sets for binary direct, indirect, total, and overall effects under two-stage randomization and stratified partial interference are obtained by inversion of randomization tests, with a targeted approximation algorithm.
Full-neighborhood exposure probabilities can be exponentially small in degree and graph-cluster randomization can sharply reduce Horvitz--Thompson variance.
Conflict-graph connectivity controls upper and lower minimax mean-squared-error rates when the design and estimator are decision variables.
Under ordinary randomized experiments, nonasymptotic treatment-effect intervals attain the effective sample size \(n\pi\), with matching estimation-rate lower bounds.
Between-class moduli lower-bound expected confidence-interval length and ordered moduli yield procedures within constant factors in Gaussian models.
Convex regression classes admit finite-sample modulus-based optimal intervals and sharp efficiency bounds under normal errors with known variance.
Under interference, existence of unbiased estimators does not guarantee variance that decreases with population size.
Randomized fuzzy intervals attain a minimum expected-length benchmark for a one-parameter Bernoulli observation problem.

body.tldr: Unequal clique sizes turn full-neighborhood treatment and control exposure into independent nonidentical categorical reveals.  The observed-data block Horvitz--Thompson estimator has a clipped finite-sample Bernstein interval, and trimming is within a universal constant of the capped water-filling modulus.  A new common-location no-reveal argument, valid for every measurable externally randomized interval, proves \(\mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\ge \omega_\alpha(w,q)^3/(136\log(1/\alpha))\).  This cubic converse closes the exact consistency boundary \(\mathcal R_\alpha\to0\Longleftrightarrow\omega_\alpha\to0\Longleftrightarrow\rho_0\to0\), including arrays for which \(S\not\to0\).  It does not prove sharp confidence length: the former two-sided no-dominance theorem is replaced by its proved upper half, and the equal- and two-scale corollaries now state upper bounds only.  The sole remaining frontier obstruction is a universal linear weighted-erasure interval-spread converse.  The pinned \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\) diagnostic separately reports graph rejection and package-versus-reference label mismatch.

project_justification.gap: Existing partial-interference confidence procedures do not characterize worst-case expected length over every measurable externally randomized interval under fixed balanced assignment on unequal cliques.  The consistency boundary is now settled by a cubic capped-erasure lower bound.  The remaining sharp-frontier gap is singular: strengthen weighted-erasure interval spread from the proved cubic modulus to a universal linear modulus, with the tilted-sign no-dominance and capped global formulations as its two regimes.
project_justification.niche: The paper treats the known assignment distribution as the sole source of randomness and exposes two computable design scales: the quadratic rare-exposure scale for the implementable Bernstein interval and the capped water-filling or trimming scale under dominance.  The capped scale is now necessary and sufficient for consistency, while its sharp linear minimax confidence-length interpretation remains open.
project_justification.fill: The proved portion consists of the exact independent categorical block reduction, an observed-data Horvitz--Thompson estimator, a clipped Bernstein interval, a bias-protected trimmed interval, a certified capped water-filling optimizer, a constant-factor trimming dual, an exact randomized-decision embedding, and a common-location no-reveal lower bound.  Together these results give the full consistency boundary and show that \(S\to0\) is sufficient but not necessary.  The note makes only one-sided sharp-rate claims until a universal linear weighted-erasure converse is proved.

body.related_work: TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012, Section 4.3, derives finite-sample Hoeffding-type intervals for allocation-strategy effects under a two-stage partial-interference design, and RigdonHudgens2015 obtains exact confidence sets for those effects by randomization-test inversion.  Those estimands and designs differ from the fixed unequal-clique All Treat versus All Control contrast here.  AronowSamii2017 supplies the design--exposure--estimand architecture and exposure-specific inverse weighting, while UganderKarrerBackstromKleinberg2013 shows that full-neighborhood exposure probabilities may be exponentially small in degree.  BasseAiroldi2018 gives a nonconcentration warning, UganderYin2023 changes the design to mitigate small probabilities, and KandirosHarshawSavje2026 studies design-based mean-squared-error criteria rather than all-interval confidence length.  CaiLow2004 and ArmstrongKolesar2018 motivate modulus logic in Gaussian experiments, but do not supply the heterogeneous weighted-erasure interval-spread converse required here.  The new self-contained common-location argument proves the cubic lower bound needed for consistency; it is not presented as the still-missing linear sharp converse.  The pinned \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\) source uses the complement of All Treat in its second output column, so the diagnostic compares it with an independently recomputed unanimous All Control reference.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The proved common-location construction yields \(\mathcal R_\alpha\gtrsim\omega_\alpha^3/\log(1/\alpha)\), which is exactly strong enough for the fixed-confidence consistency equivalence but can be much smaller than \(\omega_\alpha\).  The no-dominance lower half and the unrestricted sharp capped lower bound therefore remain open manifestations of one problem: a universal linear weighted-erasure interval-spread converse.  Any resolution must control the relevant posterior or concentration function, compact-support boundaries, random reveal information, and external interval randomization; the exact embedding and the cubic no-reveal argument do not supply that missing linear step.
body.honest_scope: The proved results concern fixed outcomes in \([-1/2,1/2]\), known unequal disjoint clique blocks, and independent unit-level \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment.  The estimator and upper intervals are measurable from \(D\) and known design quantities.  The capped optimizer, trimming comparison, exact consistency boundary, and cubic all-procedure lower bound include arbitrary independent external interval randomization.  Sharp two-sided confidence-length rates are not claimed: under no dominance the note proves the Bernstein upper rate only, and the equal- and two-scale examples inherit only that upper conclusion.  Overlapping or nonclique neighborhoods are rejected before the software diagnostic reports an interval.
body.interpretation: The computable quantity \(\rho_0(w,q)\), equivalently the unit-budget capped modulus \(\omega_1(w,q)\), is the correct consistency diagnostic.  A rare block may make \(S\) stay bounded away from zero while carrying so little causal weight that trimming it still permits vanishing honest length.  The cubic lower bound proves that no measurable randomized interval can evade a nonvanishing capped modulus, but its constants and exponent do not determine the sharp finite-confidence length.
